75	> **Auth-boundary discipline (per [ADR 0010](adr/0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md)):** new connection-CRUD endpoints (and every protected route from here on) depend on a generic internal "current user" dependency that returns DataQ's own `User` — they must NOT read MSAL token claims directly in route/service code. Cheap now; expensive to retrofit once dozens of endpoints exist. No new abstraction layer required, just the boundary.

Enforces `(type, env)` uniqueness for orchestrator rows via a **partial unique index** `WHERE type IN ('adf','airflow')` per [#72](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/72) / ADR 0004 — datasources excluded, so Snowflake stays many-per-env. CRUD/API reused unchanged: pure adapter + registry + migration addition.)_
80	- [x] ✅ Connection re-auth endpoint — refresh expired Key Vault token — `POST /connections/{id}/reauth` (`svc.reauth_connection`): rotates the credential through `SecretStore.set` **and** verifies it via the same adapter probe as `/test`, in one step (the gap PATCH+`/test` leave open). Rotation persists before the probe, so a bad new credential surfaces as 502 `connection_test_failed`; a store-write failure is 502 `connection_secret_write_failed` with the old credential untouched. 6 TestClient tests (rotate+verify ok, failed-verify-but-rotation-persists, write-fail 502, 404, secret-required 422). Type-agnostic — applies to all six connection types
81	- [x] ✅ Review `connections.secret_ref` nullability — decide based on Airflow basic-poll / unauthenticated S3 cases ([PR #41 nit](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/41)) — **decision: keep nullable.** It's NULL for the transient flush→secret-write window (create), for credential-less auth (managed-identity/IAM-role, W7, ADR 0010/0011), and for unauthenticated sources. v1 types are all secret-bearing, but presence is enforced in the **service layer** (`test_connection` → 502 without a credential), not the schema — so W7 credential-less modes need no later migration. Reads-only, persists nothing: one aggregate query (row count + null/distinct/min/max per column) + one top-N-values query per column, then `assemble_profile`. **SQL-injection-safe** — queries are built with the **SQLAlchemy Core expression language** (`select`/`table`/`column`, dialect-quoted) so there's no raw-string SQL sink (no S608/B608/CodeQL `py/sql-injection`); identifiers are additionally allowlist-validated (`validate_identifier`, strict `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*$`) as defence-in-depth + a clean early 422, and `top_n` is `int()`-coerced. v1 → 422: non-Snowflake type (dispatch generalises Week 5), bad identifier, no schema; execution failure → 502 (adapter exception never echoed). min/max/top-values NaN-sanitised. 28 tests (22 pure: identifier allowlist incl. injection strings, compiled-SQL builders, assembly, div-by-zero, NaN; 6 endpoint via fake conn: stats, injection-422, unsupported-type-422, 502, edit-gated, no-schema-422); `suites.py` 100%, `profile_service` 90% (live `_open_connection` is the deferred warehouse seam)
135	- [x] ✅ Column profiler endpoint (ADLS / S3) — same stats via Pandas on sampled file — extended `profile_service` into a type dispatcher (`profile_connection`): SQL types → in-warehouse aggregation (unchanged), flat-file types (`adls_gen2`/`s3`) → download a **sample** of the file into Pandas and compute the same stats (`profile_dataframe`). Same `POST /suites/{id}/profile` endpoint, now polymorphic: SQL targets pass `table`/`schema`, flat-file targets pass `path` (+ optional `file_format`, else inferred from extension); response carries whichever identity applies. CSV + Parquet. **pandas "load less data" levers** (per the user's scale.html prompt): column projection (CSV `usecols`, Parquet `columns=` via pyarrow schema) so profiling 3 of N columns doesn't read all N, + row sampling (`_SAMPLE_ROWS`), + **zero-copy Arrow-backed dtypes** on the Parquet read (`dtype_backend="pyarrow"` — parquet is already Arrow, kept zero-copy; the stat helpers + `_to_native` are Arrow-scalar/`pd.NA`-safe). Stats are vectorised pandas (no Python row loops — enhancingperf N/A; CoW is a no-op for a read-only profiler + a process-global flag, so not toggled; pyarrow CSV engine rejected — it's incompatible with `nrows`/callable-`usecols`). NaN/Timestamp→JSON-safe. v1 → 422: unsupported type (UC still pending), missing target, unknown format, missing column; read failure → 502 (exception never echoed). Reuses `ColumnProfile`/`ProfileResult`. 24 new tests (pure `profile_dataframe`/`infer_file_format`/`_to_native`/projection-parse + endpoint via fake `_read_dataframe`); `suites.py` 100%, `profile_service` 85% (only the live `_open_connection`/`_download_bytes` network seams uncovered — deferred smoke). _Deferred: streaming/range reads (whole object still downloaded before sampling) + out-of-core (Dask) — future work if profiling cost bites._
136	- [x] ✅ Column profiler endpoint (Unity Catalog) — via Databricks SQL Warehouse — added `unity_catalog` to the profiler's **SQL** branch (reuses `profile_table` + the SQLAlchemy Core query builders + `assemble_profile` — no duplicate aggregation logic). `_open_connection` now dispatches the engine by type (`_engine_args`): Snowflake URL or a `REDACTED` URL via the installed `databricks` SQLAlchemy dialect. UC's **3-level namespace** (`catalog.schema.table`) is handled by building the table with a `quoted_name(f"{catalog}.{schema}", quote=False)` so the dialect emits three dotted parts rather than quoting the dotted string as one — verified by compiling the real builders against the Databricks dialect. Injection-safe: every part (catalog/schema/table/column) is allowlist-validated (no raw-string SQL, no CodeQL py/sql-injection surface). Endpoint gained `catalog` (request + response); the dispatcher requires it for UC (`422 profile_target_invalid` if absent). 12 new tests (catalog-aware builders compiled to SQL, `_engine_args` URL dispatch, UC endpoint stats via the same fake conn, missing-catalog 422, bad-catalog-identifier 422); `suites.py` 100%, `profile_service` 86% (only the live `_open_connection`/`_download_bytes` network seams uncovered — deferred smoke). **Completes the column profiler across all 4 datasources.**

138	### Flat file check specifics (2 tasks — 2/2 ✅)
139	- [x] ✅ Check types for flat files: schema validation, row count, null checks, ~~freshness by filename date~~ — `FlatFileCheckRunner` (`datasources/flatfile.py`): downloads the file (S3/ADLS) into a pandas DataFrame and runs the suite's GX expectations against GX's **pandas DataFrame asset**, so all GX expectation-kind checks (schema/row-count/null/value checks) run against flat files. Extracted the shared GX machinery — snake_case→GX-class translation, GX-result→`SuiteOutcome` mapping, and the suite/validation-definition `run_expectations` flow — into `datasources/gx_runner.py` (reused by the Snowflake runner and the future UC runner; no duplication). Flat-file IO (`download_bytes` + full-file `read_dataframe`) moved to `flatfile.py` behind primitives (raw config + resolved secret, not the ORM — matches `build_snowflake_runner`), and the column profiler now shares it. Because GX runs **in-process on the DataFrame**, the run path is fully unit-tested with a canned frame (real GX execution, not mocked) — only the network download is the deferred-smoke seam. 16 new tests; `gx_runner` 100%, `flatfile` 76% (only `download_bytes` uncovered). _Connection-type → runner dispatch (Snowflake vs flat-file) is the Week-5 `run_suite` wiring; **freshness-by-filename** is the reserved `freshness` monitor kind (deferred, ADR 0012), not a GX expectation._
140	- [x] ✅ Batch resolution — resolve batching regex to matched files, pick latest or specific batch — `resolve_batch` (`datasources/flatfile.py`): a batch `pattern` is a regex whose **first capture group is the batch key**; `latest` selects the greatest key (lexicographic — ISO dates sort chronologically), falling back to the storage modified-time when the pattern has no group; `specific` selects the file whose key equals a given `batch`. `BatchNotFoundError` on no match / unknown batch. The filter+select logic is pure and fully unit-tested (8 tests); object listing (`list_files` — S3 `list_objects_v2` paginated / ADLS `list_blobs`) is the live seam, and `resolve_batch_file` composes list+resolve. _Wiring a check's target to a resolved batch path is the Week-5 `run_suite` dispatch._

Because GX runs **in-process on the DataFrame**, the run path is unit-tested with a canned frame (real GX execution); only the reflect+read (`_read_table`) is the deferred-smoke seam. `build_unity_catalog_runner` mirrors `build_snowflake_runner` (raw config + resolved PAT, not the ORM). 14 tests; `unity_catalog` 91% (only `_read_table` uncovered). _Connection-type → runner dispatch is the Week-5 `run_suite` wiring._

## Week 5 — Execution engine + scheduling

**Milestone:** Async runs with live progress across all datasource types; scheduling operational

### Async execution backend
- [ ] Celery + Redis background task runner for GX scan execution
- [ ] Run progress API — poll endpoint returning per-check live status
- [ ] Cancel run endpoint — gracefully terminate in-progress Celery task
- [ ] Run history retention policy — configurable purge of results older than N days
- [ ] Flat file run path — resolve batch, load via Pandas, execute GX suite
- [ ] UC run path — submit job to Databricks SQL Warehouse, execute GX suite

### ADF hybrid monitoring (webhook + polling fallback)
- [ ] Celery beat task — poll ADF REST API every 10 min for **succeeded** pipeline runs and full run metadata; skip pipelines already updated by webhook within the last 10 min to avoid redundant calls
- [ ] Gap recovery logic — on startup and on a 30-min schedule, fetch all ADF run statuses for the past hour and upsert any missed events (catches webhook failures during API restarts or deploys)
- [ ] `GET /api/v1/adf/pipelines` — return latest status per pipeline (source: DB, updated by both webhook and polling); used by the UI for display

> **Design note:** Webhook handles failure events near-instantly (~1–5 min). Polling handles succeeded runs, run detail enrichment, and recovery from missed webhook calls. The UI always reads from the DB — it never calls ADF directly.

### Execution UI
- [ ] Run now panel — suite picker, env / datasource, notification target
- [ ] Live run progress UI — check-by-check status with spinner + cancel button
- [ ] Scheduled runs table — create, pause, delete cron schedules
- [ ] Recent runs audit table with drill-down link to results

---

## Week 6 — Results dashboard + alerting

**Milestone:** Full results dashboard live across all source types; alerts firing with suppression

### Results dashboard
- [ ] Health score stat cards + 7-day trend chart
- [ ] Per-suite pass / fail progress bars — updated to show warn / fail / critical breakdown
- [ ] Results filter bar — by env, datasource type, suite, date range, status (including warn / fail / critical)
- [ ] Failed check drill-down — sample failing rows from GX result
- [ ] Per-check historical trend chart (not just overall health score)
- [ ] ADF pipeline status panel — polls `GET /api/v1/adf/pipelines` every 30s; status reflects webhook-pushed failures (near real-time) and polling-filled succeeded runs; shows pipeline name, last run time, duration, status badge, and correlated DQ result
- [ ] Datasource type filter — toggle Snowflake / flat file / Unity Catalog on results view
- [ ] CSV + PDF export of results
- [ ] Severity badge colours — green (pass), amber (warn), red (fail), dark red (critical); applied consistently across all result tables, drill-downs, and suite cards
- [ ] Health score weighting — apply agreed penalty weights (warn / fail / critical) in health score calculation; show severity breakdown in the 7-day trend tooltip

### Alerting
- [ ] Notification config UI — Teams webhook per suite, alert on fail / warn / always
- [ ] Alert suppression / snooze — silence a specific check for N hours
- [ ] Alert dedup — fire on first failure only, not on every subsequent scheduled run
- [ ] Teams adaptive card payload — check name, datasource, table / file, observed vs expected
- [ ] Severity-aware alert routing — `warn` fires a quieter notification (different card colour, no @mention); `fail` fires standard alert; `critical` fires with @channel mention and distinct card styling

---

## Week 7 — Deployment, hardening & docs

**Milestone:** Production-ready v1 deployed to Azure, CI/CD live, team onboarded

### DevOps & deployment
- [ ] Containerise FastAPI + React + Celery + Redis
- [ ] Push images to Azure Container Registry
- [ ] Deploy to Azure Container Apps (API + Celery worker) + Azure Static Web App (React UI)
- [ ] CI/CD pipeline — lint, test, build, deploy on merge to `main`
- [ ] Application Insights integration — traces, errors, slow queries, Celery task metrics

### Azure Monitor webhook setup (one-time infra, post-deployment)
> Requires Azure Container Apps deployment to be live first so the public FastAPI URL is known. Requires `Microsoft.Insights/actionGroups/write` + `Microsoft.Insights/metricAlerts/write` permissions on the subscription.
- [ ] Create Action Group (pre-prod) — type: Webhook, URL: `https://<pre-prod-api>.azurecontainerapps.io/api/v1/adf/events`, shared secret: value from Key Vault
- [ ] Create Alert Rule (pre-prod) — scope: `example-adf-preprod` factory, signal: `Failed pipeline runs`, dimension: all pipelines (tick "include all future values"), action: Action Group above
- [ ] Create Action Group (prod) — same config pointing to prod API URL
- [ ] Create Alert Rule (prod) — scope: `example-adf-prod` factory, same signal + dimension config
- [ ] Smoke test — trigger a deliberate pipeline failure in DEV, confirm webhook fires, DB updates, and ADF panel reflects failure within 5 min

### FastMCP — MCP server
> **Library:** `fastmcp` (PrefectHQ). Curated hand-crafted tools mounted into the existing FastAPI app. Each tool calls the internal service layer directly — no logic duplication, but descriptions are written specifically for LLM consumption, not REST API consumers.

- [ ] Install FastMCP, scaffold `mcp_server.py`, mount MCP app into FastAPI at `/mcp` — `app.mount("/mcp", mcp.get_asgi_app())`
- [ ] Wire Azure AD token validation into FastMCP's auth provider — validate Bearer token on every MCP tool call using the same `verify_azure_ad_token` logic as the REST API

203	- [x] ✅ Generalise `run_suite` worker dispatch — select the `CheckRunner` by `connection.type` via the runner registry (`build_check_runner`), replacing the Snowflake-hardcoded wiring in `worker/tasks.py`; the seam that makes the flat-file / UC run paths route correctly and post-v1 RDBMS adapters a drop-in — [PR #146-fix](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/146) _(added per [ADR 0011](adr/0011-extensibility-seams-for-deferred-integrations.md); profiler dispatch collapsed onto a parallel registry in the same effort, [#147](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/147))_
204	- [x] ✅ **Check target table/path** — modeled as a **per-suite** datasource-shaped `Suite.target` (JSONB, shaped like the column-profiler request: `table`/`schema`/`catalog`/`path`/`file_format`), since `execute_run` runs all of a suite's checks against one batch (the GX data-asset-per-suite shape). `services/run_target.resolve_target` resolves it per connection type to the runner's `(table, schema, catalog)` triple (flat-file path rides the table-shaped `CheckRunner`'s `table` slot); `validate_target` is the write-time 422 guard on suite create/update. Migration `b1f2c3d4e5a6` (additive nullable column, tested up/down on Postgres). **Dispatch ungated**: `_trigger_suites` now hands each created run to `run_suite.delay` (lazy import — worker↔service cycle), broker-fail marks the run `failed`; `run_suite` resolves the target from the suite (targetless → clean `failed`), so the worker no longer takes a `table` arg; stale `until_week3` wording removed. 13 resolver units + worker/orchestration/suite-API target tests. _(Re-tracked from Week 3; [#215](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/215); PR-C0a)_
205	- [x] ✅ **Manual run trigger + run/result read API** — `POST /suites/{id}/run` queues a `Run` and dispatches it via the shared `run_dispatch.dispatch_run` helper (**edit**-gated — the capability ladder grants "trigger runs" at edit); the suite target (#215) is resolved **up front** so a targetless/misconfigured suite fails fast with 422 instead of a queued→failed run, and a broker outage marks the run `failed` + returns 503 (same contract as the probe). New `api/v1/runs.py` read surface for the results page: `GET /runs?suite_id=&status=&limit=` and `GET /runs/{id}` (run + joined `Result`s) are **suite-scoped** — the list filters to accessible suites and the detail gates on `require_permission(view)`, so per-suite sharing + existence-hiding hold (exactly why direct-Postgres/Grafana is rejected as the primary surface); `GET /pipeline_runs?provider=&status=` is the orchestration monitoring feed (auth-only, not suite-scoped). Read helpers live in `run_service.list_runs/get_run/list_results` + `orchestration_service.list_pipeline_runs`. 14 DB-backed API tests (trigger happy/targetless-422/edit-403/no-access-404/broker-503; list scoping+filters+limit; detail+results / 404s; pipeline filters + auth). _(Run-enablement gap; PR-C0b; gates the Week-6 Results page PR-C1)_

===== #212 =====
TITLE: create_suite accepts an orchestration connection (ADF/Airflow) as a suite target
LABELS: bug, priority/P2

Surfaced by the full-stack E2E smoke (#211 review).

## Problem
`suite_service.create_suite` validates only that `connection_id` references an existing connection — **not** that the connection is a *datasource*. So `POST /suites` with an ADF or Airflow `connection_id` returns **201**, binding a suite to an orchestration provider.

This violates the core boundary (CLAUDE.md §4 / §11): ADF + Airflow are orchestration providers, **not** queryable datasources — you can't author/run DQ checks against them. A suite bound to one is a semantically invalid, unrunnable state.

(The E2E smoke originally tripped over this — `GET /connections` is `created_at DESC`, so the last-seeded Airflow connection was `conns[0]`, and the round-trip happily created a suite on it. The smoke was fixed to pick a datasource; the backend gap remains.)

## Fix
In `create_suite` (and the suite import path), reject a `connection.type` in the orchestration set (`adf`, `airflow`) with a 422 (e.g. `suite_connection_not_datasource`). Reuse the datasource/orchestration split already encoded in the registries rather than hardcoding the two names.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `POST /suites` with an ADF/Airflow connection → 422 (not 201)
- [ ] Suite import with an orchestration connection → 422
- [ ] A datasource connection (snowflake/s3/adls_gen2/unity_catalog) still works
- [ ] Test covering the rejection

===== #122 =====
TITLE: Add operational result statuses: skip + error (additive CHECK widening)
LABELS: enhancement, priority/P1

## Context
The Week-3 schema seam ([#121](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/121)) retargeted `results.status` to ADR 0005's **severity tiers** — `pass / warn / fail / critical` — and deliberately **dropped the previously-unused `skipped`** value (it was never emitted by the run path).

That decision was explicitly made on the basis that adding operational states back later is a **cheap, additive `CHECK` widening** — the opposite of the expensive tier-*narrowing* ADR 0005 front-loaded. This issue tracks doing exactly that when the run path needs them.

## Ask
Add two **operational** (non-severity) result statuses, orthogonal to the four health-score tiers:

- **`skip`** — the check did not evaluate (e.g. not applicable to this batch, gated off, batch/file missing).
- **`error`** — the check threw / could not be evaluated (distinct from `fail`, which is a *successful evaluation* that breached an expectation). Today a per-check exception drives the whole **run** to `failed` (`run_service`); a per-result `error` lets a single check error without failing siblings.

## Implementation notes
- Additive migration: widen the `ck_results_status_valid` CHECK to `('pass','warn','fail','critical','skip','error')`. No data rewrite, no two-step (pure widening).
- Add to `RESULT_STATUSES` in `db/models.py`.
- **Health-score SQL must exclude `skip`/`error` from `N`** — they carry no penalty weight (ADR 0005 only defines weights for the four tiers). i.e. aggregate `WHERE status IN ('pass','warn','fail','critical')`.
- `run_service` (and the future `check.kind` dispatch / severity post-processing) emit them where appropriate.

## When
Pick up alongside the run-path work that first produces them — severity post-processing / `check.kind` dispatch (Week 3) or the execution-engine hardening (Week 5). Not blocking; the seam was left intentionally cheap to extend.

Refs: ADR 0005 (severity tiers), ADR 0012 (`check.kind`), PR #121 (the drop decision).

===== #227 =====
TITLE: Dedupe the create-queued-run + dispatch + broker-failure pattern across trigger paths
LABELS: priority/P3, refactor

## Context
Three sites create a queued `Run`, hand it to `run_dispatch.dispatch_run`, and on broker failure mark it terminal-`failed`:
- `api/v1/probe.py` `trigger_snowflake_probe`
- `api/v1/suites.py` `trigger_suite_run` (manual run, PR-C0b #225)
- `services/orchestration_service.py` `_trigger_suites` (pipeline-success, batch)

The broker-failure DB shape had **already diverged** once: `_trigger_suites` set `status=failed` **and** `finished_at=now()`, while `probe` and the new manual path set only `status`. PR-C0b aligned the manual path (finished_at set), but `probe.py` still leaves `finished_at` NULL, and the create+dispatch+503 block is duplicated.

## Ask
Extract a shared helper (e.g. `run_dispatch.create_and_dispatch_run(session, *, suite_id, triggered_by) -> Run`, or a `mark_dispatch_failed(run)` for the failure shape) so the terminal-failed contract is one decision. Note: `_trigger_suites` dispatches a **batch** in a loop, so the helper must fit that shape or split into create vs failure-shape pieces.

## Acceptance
- One definition of the dispatch-failure run shape; `probe.py` aligned (finished_at set).
- No behaviour change to happy paths; existing tests stay green.

_Surfaced by the PR-C0b multi-agent review (altitude/reuse)._

===== #147 =====
TITLE: Profiler / flat-file cleanup: timeout drift, duplicated format+stat logic, N+1 profiler queries
LABELS: priority/P1, refactor

Low-priority cleanup items surfaced during the full `/code-review` of `58193cd..HEAD` (column profiler + check runners, #137–#144). Grouped here; none is a correctness bug. The correctness/robustness findings are tracked separately in #145, and the dispatch/registry gap in #146.

### 1. S3 read-timeout drift (30s → 60s)
When the flat-file download was extracted into `flatfile.py`, the S3 read timeout changed from the profiler's original 30s (`profile_service._NETWORK_TIMEOUT`) to [`_READ_TIMEOUT = 60`](backend/app/datasources/flatfile.py#L38). More lenient than before; a hung S3 read now ties up a worker thread twice as long. Confirm 60s is intentional (full-file reads may legitimately need longer than a profiler sample) vs accidental drift, and align the two constants.

### 2. `_SUPPORTED_FORMATS` duplicates `format_from_path`
[`infer_file_format`](backend/app/services/profile_service.py#L333) calls `flatfile.format_from_path(path)` then checks membership in [`_SUPPORTED_FORMATS = {"csv","parquet"}`](backend/app/services/profile_service.py#L62). But `format_from_path` already only ever returns `csv`/`parquet`/`None`, so the supported-format set is expressed twice. Add JSON to `format_from_path` and the profiler silently still rejects it. Derive the supported set from `format_from_path`, or drop the redundant check.

### 3. Duplicated stat contract: SQL vs pandas
The per-column statistic definitions (null_fraction = nulls/row_count with the row_count==0 guard, distinct excludes nulls, top_values = non-null desc by count) are implemented twice with no shared code — once in SQL via [`assemble_profile`](backend/app/services/profile_service.py#L195) and once in pandas via [`profile_dataframe`](backend/app/services/profile_service.py#L362). A definitional change must be made in both or the two datasource families disagree for the same logical data. (Hard to fully DRY across SQL vs pandas, but the *contract* could be captured in one place / a shared test.)

### 4. N+1 warehouse round-trips in the SQL profiler
[`profile_table`](backend/app/services/profile_service.py#L304) issues 1 aggregate query + one top-values query **per column** in a Python loop. For a 50-column profile that's 51 sequential warehouse queries; against a cold SQL warehouse (~1s/query) that's ~50s of wall time for an interactive authoring aid. Acceptable for v1 (≤50-col cap), but consider batching the top-values queries (UNION ALL / a single windowed query) if profiler latency becomes a problem.

### 5. Parquet footer read twice (minor)
[`_read_dataframe`](backend/app/services/profile_service.py#L440) reads `pq.ParquetFile(raw).schema.names` to filter requested columns to those present, then re-parses with `pd.read_parquet(columns=present)`. The footer read is cheap, and it's needed so `read_parquet` doesn't raise on an absent column — but the column-presence logic now lives in two places (the pre-read filter and `profile_dataframe`'s missing-column 422 check). Worth a glance to ensure they can't diverge.

Pick up opportunistically; suggest a single cleanup PR (`Fixes #<this>`).

43	    The suite's datasource-shaped ``target`` (#215) resolves to the runner's
44	    ``(table, schema, catalog)`` via ``run_target.resolve_target``; dispatch by
45	    ``connection.type`` through the runner registry gives a Snowflake / Unity
46	    Catalog / flat-file suite its correct `CheckRunner` (#146).
47	
48	    Failures while loading, resolving the target (targetless or malformed suite),
49	    or building the runner (missing rows, bad connection config, unresolved
50	    secret) drive the run to ``failed`` so it never lingers in ``queued``;
51	    execution failures are handled inside ``execute_run``.
52	    """
53	    run = session.get(Run, run_id)
54	    if run is None:
55	        log.error("run_suite_run_not_found", run_id=str(run_id))
56	        return "not_found"
57	
58	    try:
59	        suite = session.get(Suite, run.suite_id)
60	        connection = session.get(Connection, suite.connection_id) if suite is not None else None
61	        if suite is None or connection is None:
62	            raise RuntimeError("suite or connection not found for run")
63	        target = run_target.resolve_target(connection.type, suite.target)
64	        checks = list(session.scalars(select(Check).where(Check.suite_id == suite.id)))
65	        runner = build_check_runner(
66	            conn_type=connection.type,
67	            config=connection.config,
68	            secret_ref=connection.secret_ref,
69	            secret_store=get_secret_store(),
70	            catalog=target.catalog,
71	        )
72	    except Exception:
73	        run.status = "failed"
74	        run.started_at = run.started_at or datetime.now(UTC)
75	        run.finished_at = datetime.now(UTC)
76	        session.commit()
77	        log.exception("run_suite_setup_failed", run_id=str(run_id))
78	        return "failed"
79	
80	    run_service.execute_run(
81	        session, run=run, checks=checks, runner=runner, table=target.table, schema=target.schema
82	    )
83	    return str(run.status)
84	
85	
86	@celery_app.task(name="run_suite")  # type: ignore[untyped-decorator]  # celery task decorator is unannotated
87	def run_suite(run_id: str) -> str:
88	    """Worker entry point. ``run_id`` is a string so it serialises over JSON.
89	
90	    The target is resolved from the suite (``Suite.target``), so the only
91	    argument the dispatcher supplies is the run id.
92	    """
93	    session = get_session()
94	    try:
95	        return _run_suite(session, run_id=uuid.UUID(run_id))
96	    finally:
97	        session.close()
98	
99	
100	def _poll_orchestration_runs(
101	    session: Session, *, secret_store: SecretStore, now: datetime | None = None
102	) -> dict[str, int]:
103	    """Poll every orchestrator connection for recent succeeded runs (#171, ADR 0004).
104	
105	    The polling fallback for runs that never produced a webhook: iterate each
106	    ADF / Airflow connection, ask the provider's `list_recent_runs` for runs
107	    updated within the lookback window, and hand them to `ingest_polled_runs`
108	    (upsert + trigger-on-success). Goes through the `OrchestrationProvider` seam —
109	    no per-provider branching. Each connection is isolated: a transport/auth
110	    failure logs + continues so one bad connection can't starve the rest.
111	    """
112	    since = (now or datetime.now(UTC)) - _POLL_LOOKBACK
113	    summary = {"connections": 0, "recorded": 0, "triggered": 0, "skipped": 0, "errors": 0}
114	    connections = list(
115	        session.scalars(
116	            select(Connection).where(
117	                Connection.type.in_(ORCHESTRATION_PROVIDERS),
118	                Connection.secret_ref.isnot(None),
119	            )
120	        )
121	    )
122	    for connection in connections:
123	        if not connection.secret_ref:  # defensive; the query already filters
124	            continue
125	        try:
126	            provider_impl = get_orchestration_provider(connection.type)
127	            secret = secret_store.get(connection.secret_ref)
128	            updates = provider_impl.list_recent_runs(dict(connection.config), secret, since)
129	            result = orchestration_service.ingest_polled_runs(
130	                session,
131	                provider_impl=provider_impl,
132	                connection=connection,
133	                updates=updates,
134	                skip_updated_since=since,
135	            )
136	            summary["connections"] += 1
137	            summary["recorded"] += len(result.pipeline_runs)
138	            summary["triggered"] += len(result.triggered_runs)
139	            summary["skipped"] += result.skipped
140	        except Exception:
141	            summary["errors"] += 1
142	            session.rollback()
143	            log.exception(
144	                "orchestration_poll_failed",
145	                connection_id=str(connection.id),
146	                provider=connection.type,
147	            )
148	    log.info("orchestration_poll_completed", **summary)
149	    return summary
150	
151	
152	@celery_app.task(name="poll_orchestration_runs")  # type: ignore[untyped-decorator]  # celery task decorator is unannotated
153	def poll_orchestration_runs() -> dict[str, int]:
154	    """Celery-beat entry point — the 10-min orchestration polling fallback."""
155	    session = get_session()
156	    try:
157	        return _poll_orchestration_runs(session, secret_store=get_secret_store())
158	    finally:
159	        session.close()
160

1	"""Execute a suite's checks via a datasource adapter and persist the results.
2	
3	This is the GX-agnostic core of a run: it drives the `Run` lifecycle, calls a
4	`CheckRunner` (injected — Snowflake in production, a fake in tests), and maps the
5	returned `SuiteOutcome` onto `Result` rows. GX/Snowflake specifics live behind
6	the adapter; this layer only knows the DTOs in ``datasources.base``.
7	
8	Run.status describes *execution*, not data quality: a run that completes is
9	``succeeded`` even when checks fail (the failures live in ``Result.status`` /
10	``SuiteOutcome.success``). ``failed`` means the run could not execute — the
11	adapter raised (e.g. could not reach the warehouse).
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import uuid
17	from datetime import UTC, datetime
18	
19	from sqlalchemy import select
20	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
21	
22	from backend.app.core.jsonsafe import sanitize_json
23	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
24	from backend.app.datasources.base import CheckOutcome, CheckRunner, CheckSpec
25	from backend.app.db.models import Check, Result, Run
26	from backend.app.services import suite_service
27	from backend.app.services.severity import derive_status, extract_metric
28	
29	log = get_logger(__name__)
30	
31	
32	def _now() -> datetime:
33	    return datetime.now(UTC)
34	
35	
36	def _build_result(run_id: uuid.UUID, check: Check, outcome: CheckOutcome) -> Result:
37	    """Map a check + its GX outcome to a `Result`, deriving the severity tier.
38	
39	    The unexpected-percent badness scalar is extracted once and used both to band
40	    the tier (ADR 0005 / 0016) and to persist as the durable, SQL-aggregatable
41	    `metric_value` (ADR 0012). `duration_ms` stays NULL in v1 — per-check timing
42	    isn't separable from GX's single suite-level `validate()` (reserved seam).
43	    """
44	    metric = extract_metric(outcome)
45	    status = derive_status(
46	        success=outcome.success,
47	        metric_value=metric,
48	        warn_threshold=check.warn_threshold,
49	        fail_threshold=check.fail_threshold,
50	        critical_threshold=check.critical_threshold,
51	    )
52	    return Result(
53	        run_id=run_id,
54	        check_id=check.id,
55	        status=status,
56	        metric_value=metric,
57	        observed_value=sanitize_json(outcome.observed_value),
58	        expected_value=sanitize_json(outcome.expected_value),
59	        sample_failures=sanitize_json(outcome.sample_failures),
60	    )
61	
62	
63	_EXPECTATION_KIND = "expectation"
64	
65	
66	def _specs_for_checks(checks: list[Check]) -> list[CheckSpec]:
67	    """Dispatch checks by `check.kind` to their runner input (ADR 0012).
68	
69	    v1 implements only the `expectation` kind (the GX `CheckRunner`). The other
70	    reserved kinds (`freshness`/`volume`/`schema_drift`/`anomaly`/`comparison`)
71	    are constraint-valid but have no runner yet, so a run containing one raises
72	    `NotImplementedError` rather than silently feeding it to GX as an
73	    expectation. This dispatch composes with the connection-type `CheckRunner`
74	    selection (Week 5, ADR 0011): `kind` chooses the *monitor*, `connection.type`
75	    chooses the *adapter*.
76	    """
77	    unsupported = sorted({c.kind for c in checks if c.kind != _EXPECTATION_KIND})
78	    if unsupported:
79	        raise NotImplementedError(
80	            f"no run path for check kind(s) {', '.join(unsupported)}; "
81	            f"only {_EXPECTATION_KIND!r} is implemented in v1"
82	        )
83	    return [CheckSpec(expectation_type=c.expectation_type, kwargs=dict(c.config)) for c in checks]
84	
85	
86	def execute_run(
87	    session: Session,
88	    *,
89	    run: Run,
90	    checks: list[Check],
91	    runner: CheckRunner,
92	    table: str,
93	    schema: str | None = None,
94	) -> Run:
95	    """Run ``checks`` against ``table`` via ``runner`` and persist the outcome.
96	
97	    ``run`` must already be persisted (it carries the id the results link to).
98	    Returns the same `Run`, updated to ``succeeded`` or ``failed``.
99	    """
100	    run.status = "running"
101	    run.started_at = _now()
102	    session.commit()
103	    log.info(
104	        "run_started",
105	        run_id=str(run.id),
106	        suite_id=str(run.suite_id),
107	        n_checks=len(checks),
108	        table=table,
109	    )
110	
111	    # Everything from here — dispatching by kind, running the adapter, building
112	    # rows, and persisting them — is guarded so any failure drives the run to a
113	    # terminal 'failed' state. Without this, a DB error during add_all/commit (or
114	    # an unrunnable check kind) would leave the run stuck in 'running' forever.
115	    # rollback() discards any partial result inserts before we record the failure.
116	    try:
117	        specs = _specs_for_checks(checks)
118	        outcome = runner.run_checks(table=table, schema=schema, checks=specs)
119	        rows = [
120	            _build_result(run.id, check, check_outcome)
121	            for check, check_outcome in zip(checks, outcome.checks, strict=True)
122	        ]
123	        session.add_all(rows)
124	        run.status = "succeeded"
125	        run.finished_at = _now()
126	        session.commit()
127	    except Exception:
128	        session.rollback()
129	        run.status = "failed"
130	        run.finished_at = _now()
131	        session.commit()
132	        log.exception("run_failed", run_id=str(run.id), table=table)
133	        return run
134	
135	    log.info(
136	        "run_completed",
137	        run_id=str(run.id),
138	        suite_success=outcome.success,
139	        n_results=len(rows),
140	    )
141	    return run
142	
143	
144	# ── read model (PR-C0b: the runs/results surface) ────────────────────────────
145	# Reads are scoped to suites the user can access — owned (`created_by`) or shared
146	# (`shares`), the same visibility `suite_service.list_suites` enforces. The API
147	# layer additionally calls `require_permission` for single-suite / single-run
148	# lookups (404 hides existence); this subquery is the defence-in-depth filter so
149	# a list query can never leak a run from a suite the caller can't see.
150	
151	
152	def list_runs(
153	    session: Session,
154	    *,
155	    user_id: uuid.UUID,
156	    suite_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
157	    status: str | None = None,
158	    limit: int = 50,
159	) -> list[Run]:
160	    """Runs for suites the user can access, newest first (`created_at` desc).
161	
162	    Optionally narrowed to one ``suite_id`` and/or a ``status``. The accessible
163	    subquery is always applied, so passing a ``suite_id`` the user can't see
164	    yields an empty list (the API layer 404s that case up front via
165	    `require_permission`, but the filter keeps the service safe on its own).
166	    """
167	    accessible = suite_service.accessible_suite_ids(user_id)
168	    stmt = (
169	        select(Run).where(Run.suite_id.in_(accessible)).order_by(Run.created_at.desc()).limit(limit)
170	    )
171	    if suite_id is not None:
172	        stmt = stmt.where(Run.suite_id == suite_id)
173	    if status is not None:
174	        stmt = stmt.where(Run.status == status)
175	    return list(session.scalars(stmt))
176	
177	
178	def get_run(session: Session, run_id: uuid.UUID) -> Run | None:
179	    """Fetch a run by id (no authz — the API layer gates on the run's suite)."""
180	    return session.get(Run, run_id)
181	
182	
183	def list_results(session: Session, run_id: uuid.UUID) -> list[Result]:
184	    """The result rows for a run, in stable check order (`created_at`)."""
185	    return list(
186	        session.scalars(select(Result).where(Result.run_id == run_id).order_by(Result.created_at))
187	    )
188

1	"""Dispatch a persisted `Run` to the Celery worker — the one place that publishes.
2	
3	Publishes ``run_suite`` **by name** via ``celery_app.send_task`` rather than
4	importing the task object. That decoupling is deliberate: ``worker.tasks``
5	imports service modules (e.g. ``orchestration_service``), so a service importing
6	``worker.tasks`` back would be a cyclic import (CodeQL `py/cyclic-import`). By
7	name there is no import edge service → worker, and the broker resolves the task
8	on the worker side. The ``before_task_publish`` signal still fires, so the
9	``request_id`` correlation header is carried exactly as for ``.delay``.
10	
11	Raises on a broker/publish failure; the caller owns the policy for a stuck run
12	(the probe endpoint surfaces 503; the pipeline-trigger path marks the run
13	``failed`` so it isn't left ``queued``).
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	import uuid
19	
20	from backend.app.worker.celery_app import celery_app
21	
22	_RUN_SUITE_TASK = "run_suite"
23	
24	
25	def dispatch_run(run_id: uuid.UUID) -> None:
26	    """Publish the ``run_suite`` task for ``run_id``. Raises if the broker is down."""
27	    celery_app.send_task(_RUN_SUITE_TASK, args=[str(run_id)])

1	"""Resolve a suite's datasource-shaped target to the runner's (table, schema, catalog).
2	
3	A suite's `target` (#215) is a small JSONB document shaped like the column
4	profiler request (``table`` / ``schema`` / ``catalog`` / ``path`` /
5	``file_format``), datasource-typed. The `CheckRunner` interface is *table-shaped*
6	— for a flat-file datasource the file path rides the ``table`` argument
7	(``flatfile.py``) — so every datasource resolves to the same triple the worker
8	hands to ``run_service.execute_run`` and ``build_check_runner``:
9	
10	    snowflake      → table (+ schema)
11	    unity_catalog  → table (+ schema) + catalog        (catalog.schema.table)
12	    adls_gen2 / s3 → path  (carried as `table`; schema/catalog unused)
13	
14	`resolve_target` is the run-time path (raises if a required field is missing).
15	`validate_target` is the write-time path (same rules; used by `suite_service`
16	when a target is set on a suite, so a malformed/wrong-datasource target is a
17	clean 422 at save rather than a failed run later).
18	
19	FastAPI-free: takes a connection type + the stored dict, raises `DataQError`.
20	"""
21	
22	from __future__ import annotations
23	
24	from dataclasses import dataclass
25	from typing import Any
26	
27	from backend.app.core.errors import DataQError
28	
29	_FLATFILE_TYPES = {"adls_gen2", "s3"}
30	
31	
32	class SuiteTargetInvalidError(DataQError):
33	    status_code = 422
34	    code = "suite_target_invalid"
35	
36	
37	@dataclass(frozen=True)
38	class ResolvedTarget:
39	    """The runner inputs a suite resolves to. ``table`` carries the file path for
40	    flat-file datasources; ``catalog`` is set only for Unity Catalog."""
41	
42	    table: str
43	    schema: str | None
44	    catalog: str | None
45	
46	
47	def resolve_target(conn_type: str, target: dict[str, Any] | None) -> ResolvedTarget:
48	    """Resolve ``target`` for a ``conn_type`` connection, or raise (422).
49	
50	    Raises `SuiteTargetInvalidError` if the suite is targetless, the target is
51	    missing the field its datasource requires (`path` for flat files, `table`
52	    for SQL, `catalog` for Unity Catalog), or the connection type has no run path
53	    (orchestration providers — they are never suite datasources).
54	    """
55	    if not target:
56	        raise SuiteTargetInvalidError(
57	            "suite has no target configured", detail={"connection_type": conn_type}
58	        )
59	
60	    if conn_type in _FLATFILE_TYPES:
61	        path = _require(target, "path", conn_type)
62	        return ResolvedTarget(table=path, schema=None, catalog=None)
63	
64	    if conn_type == "snowflake":
65	        table = _require(target, "table", conn_type)
66	        return ResolvedTarget(table=table, schema=_str_or_none(target.get("schema")), catalog=None)
67	
68	    if conn_type == "unity_catalog":
69	        table = _require(target, "table", conn_type)
70	        catalog = _require(target, "catalog", conn_type)
71	        return ResolvedTarget(
72	            table=table, schema=_str_or_none(target.get("schema")), catalog=catalog
73	        )
74	
75	    raise SuiteTargetInvalidError(
76	        f"connection type {conn_type!r} has no run path (not a datasource)",
77	        detail={"connection_type": conn_type},
78	    )
79	
80	
81	def validate_target(conn_type: str, target: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
82	    """Write-time guard: a non-null target must resolve for its datasource.
83	
84	    Reuses `resolve_target`'s rules so a target saved on a suite is always
85	    runnable. Callers only invoke this when a target is *provided* — a suite may
86	    be created/updated targetless (NULL), which is valid-but-not-yet-runnable.
87	    """
88	    resolve_target(conn_type, target)
89	
90	
91	def _require(target: dict[str, Any], field: str, conn_type: str) -> str:
92	    value = target.get(field)
93	    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
94	        raise SuiteTargetInvalidError(
95	            f"target for a {conn_type!r} suite requires a non-empty {field!r}",
96	            detail={"connection_type": conn_type, "missing": field},
97	        )
98	    return value
99	
100	
101	def _str_or_none(value: Any) -> str | None:
102	    return value if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip() else None
103

1	"""Celery application for DataQ's async execution backbone.
2	
3	GX suite runs are dispatched from FastAPI and executed here so the request
4	thread returns immediately (run created as ``queued``, worker drives it to
5	``running`` → ``succeeded``/``failed``).
6	
7	The CLAUDE.md observability rule requires ``request_id`` correlation to flow
8	FastAPI → Celery → GX. We carry it on the task message headers: the caller
9	injects the active request_id on publish, and the worker restores it into the
10	same ``request_id_var`` ContextVar the structlog processor chain reads from, so
11	worker log lines correlate with the request that triggered them.
12	"""
13	
14	from typing import Any
15	
16	from celery import Celery
17	from celery.signals import (
18	    before_task_publish,
19	    setup_logging,
20	    task_postrun,
21	    task_prerun,
22	)
23	
24	from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
25	from backend.app.core.logging import configure_logging, request_id_var
26	
27	# Message-header key carrying the originating request_id across the broker.
28	REQUEST_ID_HEADER = "request_id"
29	# Attribute on task.request where prerun stashes the ContextVar reset handle
30	# for postrun. Deliberately avoids the word "token" so it isn't mistaken for a
31	# secret by Bandit / Ruff (B105 / S105).
32	_REQUEST_ID_RESET_ATTR = "_dataq_request_id_reset"
33	
34	
35	def create_celery_app() -> Celery:
36	    settings = get_settings()
37	    app = Celery(
38	        "dataq",
39	        broker=settings.redis_url,
40	        backend=settings.redis_url,
41	    )
42	    app.conf.update(
43	        task_serializer="json",
44	        result_serializer="json",
45	        accept_content=["json"],
46	        timezone="UTC",
47	        enable_utc=True,
48	        # Surface a 'started' state so the run-status read-back can distinguish
49	        # queued from running without waiting for completion.
50	        task_track_started=True,
51	        # Celery-beat schedule. The orchestration polling fallback (#171) runs
52	        # every 10 min as the success channel for runs that produced no webhook;
53	        # the task looks back further than the interval so nothing slips the gap.
54	        # Beat runs embedded in the dev worker (`worker -B`); prod uses a separate
55	        # beat process.
56	        beat_schedule={
57	            "poll-orchestration-runs": {
58	                "task": "poll_orchestration_runs",
59	                "schedule": 600.0,  # 10 minutes
60	            },
61	        },
62	    )
63	    # Register task modules on worker boot (looks for backend.app.worker.tasks).
64	    app.autodiscover_tasks(["backend.app.worker"])
65	    return app
66	
67	
68	celery_app = create_celery_app()
69	
70	
71	@setup_logging.connect  # type: ignore[untyped-decorator]  # celery signal .connect is unannotated
72	def _configure_celery_logging(**_kwargs: Any) -> None:
73	    """Disable Celery's default logging and route worker logs through structlog.
74	
75	    Connecting any receiver to ``setup_logging`` tells Celery not to configure
76	    logging itself, so our JSON + PII-redacting processor chain stays in force
77	    inside the worker exactly as it is in the API.
78	    """
79	    configure_logging()
80	
81	
82	@before_task_publish.connect  # type: ignore[untyped-decorator]  # celery signal .connect is unannotated
83	def _inject_request_id(headers: dict[str, Any] | None = None, **_kwargs: Any) -> None:
84	    """Caller side (FastAPI): stamp the active request_id onto task headers."""
85	    if headers is None:
86	        return
87	    rid = request_id_var.get()
88	    if rid is not None:
89	        headers[REQUEST_ID_HEADER] = rid
90	
91	
92	@task_prerun.connect  # type: ignore[untyped-decorator]  # celery signal .connect is unannotated
93	def _restore_request_id(task: Any = None, **_kwargs: Any) -> None:
94	    """Worker side: restore request_id from the message into the ContextVar.
95	
96	    Custom headers added in ``before_task_publish`` are exposed as attributes on
97	    ``task.request`` under the protocol-v2 message format. We stash the reset
98	    token on ``task.request`` so ``task_postrun`` can restore the *prior* value
99	    rather than blindly clearing — under ``task_always_eager`` these signals run
100	    in the caller's context, so a blanket reset would drop the request_id for
101	    the rest of the request handler.
102	    """
103	    rid = getattr(task.request, REQUEST_ID_HEADER, None) if task is not None else None
104	    if rid and task is not None:
105	        token = request_id_var.set(rid)
106	        setattr(task.request, _REQUEST_ID_RESET_ATTR, token)
107	
108	
109	@task_postrun.connect  # type: ignore[untyped-decorator]  # celery signal .connect is unannotated
110	def _clear_request_id(task: Any = None, **_kwargs: Any) -> None:
111	    """Worker side: restore the ContextVar to its pre-task value.
112	
113	    Only resets when ``task_prerun`` actually set it (token present), mirroring
114	    the ``reset(token)`` pattern used by ``request_id_middleware`` in main.py.
115	    """
116	    token = getattr(task.request, _REQUEST_ID_RESET_ATTR, None) if task is not None else None
117	    if token is not None:
118	        request_id_var.reset(token)
119

1	"""Flat-file (ADLS Gen2 / S3) IO + GX `CheckRunner`.
2	
3	Two responsibilities for the flat-file datasources, both behind the same
4	primitives the SQL adapters use (raw config dict + resolved secret, never the ORM
5	row — keeps `datasources/` decoupled from `db/`):
6	
7	* **IO** — `download_bytes` fetches an object/blob; `read_dataframe` parses it
8	  into pandas. Shared by the column profiler (service layer) and the runner.
9	* **Runner** — `FlatFileCheckRunner` runs GX expectations against the file by
10	  loading it into an in-memory pandas DataFrame and handing that to GX's pandas
11	  datasource, then mapping the result via the shared `gx_runner` machinery. The
12	  `CheckRunner` interface is table-shaped; for a flat-file datasource the
13	  ``table`` argument carries the **file path** and ``schema`` is unused.
14	
15	GX runs entirely in-process on the DataFrame, so — unlike the warehouse runners —
16	the run path is fully testable with a canned frame; only the network download is
17	the deferred-smoke seam.
18	"""
19

36	# Connector timeouts (seconds): fail fast rather than hang the worker thread.
37	# _READ_TIMEOUT is deliberately longer than the SQL profiler's network timeout
38	# (profile_service._NETWORK_TIMEOUT = 30): it covers a full-object download (the
39	# whole CSV/Parquet is pulled before parsing), not a single warehouse query, so a
40	# large file legitimately needs more headroom. Not accidental drift (#147).
41	_CONNECT_TIMEOUT = 10
42	_READ_TIMEOUT = 60
43	
44	_FILE_TYPES = {"adls_gen2", "s3"}

51	    """Infer the file format from the path extension (`None` if unrecognised)."""
52	    lower = path.lower()
53	    if lower.endswith(".csv"):
54	        return "csv"
55	    if lower.endswith((".parquet", ".pq")):

61	    """A boto3 S3 client for `cfg` with the standard fail-fast timeouts."""

63	    from botocore.config import Config
64	
65	    return boto3.client(
66	        "s3",
67	        region_name=cfg.region,
68	        aws_access_key_id=cfg.access_key_id,
69	        aws_secret_access_key=secret,
70	        config=Config(connect_timeout=_CONNECT_TIMEOUT, read_timeout=_READ_TIMEOUT),
71	    )

75	    """An ADLS `BlobServiceClient` for `acfg` (caller must `.close()` it)."""

78	    return BlobServiceClient(account_url=acfg.account_url, credential=secret)

81	def download_bytes(*, conn_type: str, config: dict[str, Any], path: str, secret: str) -> bytes:
82	    """Fetch the object/blob bytes from S3 or ADLS Gen2 (live seam).
83	
84	    Takes the connection's `type` + raw `config` + resolved `secret` (the caller
85	    owns the SecretStore), so this module never touches the DB.
86	    """
87	    if conn_type == "s3":
88	        cfg = S3Config.model_validate(config)

92	    acfg = AdlsConfig.model_validate(config)
93	    client_az = _blob_service(acfg, secret)

102	def read_dataframe(*, conn_type: str, config: dict[str, Any], path: str, secret: str) -> Any:
103	    """Download and parse the **whole** file into a pandas DataFrame (live seam).
104	
105	    The runner reads the full file — every row and column — because a check may
106	    reference any column and row-count/null checks must be exact (unlike the
107	    profiler, which samples + projects). Raises `ValueError` for an unknown
108	    format.

115	    raw = io.BytesIO(download_bytes(conn_type=conn_type, config=config, path=path, secret=secret))
116	    if fmt == "csv":

118	    return pd.read_parquet(raw, dtype_backend="pyarrow")

121	class FlatFileCheckRunner:
122	    """`CheckRunner` for flat files — loads the file into pandas, runs GX on it.
123	
124	    Holds the resolved credential (like `SnowflakeCheckRunner` holds its
125	    connection string), so `run_checks` is self-contained. ``table`` is the file
126	    path; ``schema`` is ignored (flat files have no schema namespace).
127	    """
128	
129	    def __init__(self, *, conn_type: str, config: dict[str, Any], secret: str) -> None:
130	        self._conn_type = conn_type
131	        self._config = config
132	        self._secret = secret
133	
134	    def run_checks(
135	        self, *, table: str, schema: str | None, checks: list[CheckSpec]
136	    ) -> SuiteOutcome:
137	        df = read_dataframe(
138	            conn_type=self._conn_type, config=self._config, path=table, secret=self._secret
139	        )
140	        context = gx.get_context(mode="ephemeral")
141	        asset = context.data_sources.add_pandas(name="flatfile").add_dataframe_asset(name="file")
142	        # The pandas asset takes its batch at run time via batch_parameters; the
143	        # ephemeral context makes the fixed suite/vd names safe across runs.
144	        batch_definition = asset.add_batch_definition_whole_dataframe(name="whole_dataframe")
145	        return run_expectations(
146	            context,
147	            batch_definition=batch_definition,
148	            checks=checks,
149	            name="suite-flatfile",
150	            batch_parameters={"dataframe": df},
151	        )
152

154	def build_flatfile_runner(
155	    *, conn_type: str, config: dict[str, Any], secret_ref: str | None, secret_store: SecretStore
156	) -> FlatFileCheckRunner:
157	    """Build a runner from a flat-file `Connection`'s primitives.
158	
159	    Mirrors `build_snowflake_runner`: resolves the secret eagerly and takes the
160	    raw config (not the ORM model) to keep the adapter decoupled from `db/`.
161	    """
162	    if conn_type not in _FILE_TYPES:
163	        raise ValueError(f"{conn_type!r} is not a flat-file datasource")
164	    if not secret_ref:
165	        raise ValueError("flat-file connection requires secret_ref for the credential")
166	    secret = secret_store.get(secret_ref)
167	    return FlatFileCheckRunner(conn_type=conn_type, config=config, secret=secret)
168	
169	
170	# ───────────────────────── batch resolution ────────────────────────
171	#
172	# Flat files usually arrive in batches — `orders_2026-06-01.csv`,
173	# `orders_2026-06-02.csv`, … — and a check targets *one* batch. The batch
174	# pattern is a regex whose **first capture group is the batch key**; `latest`
175	# selects the greatest key, `specific` selects a named key. Resolution (filter +
176	# select) is pure and fully tested; only the object listing is a live seam.
177	
178	
179	class BatchNotFoundError(ValueError):
180	    """No file matched the batch pattern (or the requested specific batch)."""
181	
182	
183	@dataclass(frozen=True)
184	class FileRef:
185	    """A listed object: its full key/blob path and last-modified time (if any)."""
186	
187	    path: str
188	    last_modified: datetime | None = None
189	
190	
191	def _most_recent(files: list[FileRef]) -> str:
192	    """Path of the most recently modified file (ties broken by path; `files` non-empty)."""
193	    return max(files, key=lambda f: (f.last_modified or _MIN_DT, f.path)).path
194	
195	
196	def resolve_batch(
197	    files: list[FileRef], *, pattern: str, strategy: str = "latest", batch: str | None = None
198	) -> str:
199	    """Pick one file's path from `files` per the batch `pattern` + `strategy`.
200	
201	    `pattern` is a regex `re.search`-ed against each path; its first capture group
202	    (if any) is the batch key. `strategy`:
203	
204	    * ``latest`` — the greatest batch key (lexicographic — ISO dates sort right),
205	      or, when the pattern has no capture group, the most recently modified file.
206	    * ``specific`` — the file whose batch key equals `batch` (required).
207	
208	    Raises `BatchNotFoundError` (nothing matched / no such batch) or `ValueError`
209	    (bad strategy, or `specific` without `batch`).
210	    """
211	    try:
212	        compiled = re.compile(pattern)
213	    except re.error as exc:
214	        raise ValueError(f"invalid batch pattern {pattern!r}: {exc}") from exc
215	    matches = [(f, m) for f in files if (m := compiled.search(f.path))]
216	    if not matches:
217	        raise BatchNotFoundError(f"no files matched batch pattern {pattern!r}")
218	
219	    if strategy == "specific":
220	        if batch is None:
221	            raise ValueError("strategy 'specific' requires a batch key")
222	        hits = [f for f, m in matches if m.groups() and m.group(1) == batch]
223	        if not hits:
224	            raise BatchNotFoundError(f"no file for batch {batch!r} under pattern {pattern!r}")
225	        return _most_recent(hits)
226	
227	    if strategy != "latest":
228	        raise ValueError(f"unknown batch strategy {strategy!r}")
229	
230	    # A batch key is the first capture group when it *participated* in the match;
231	    # an optional group that didn't (`None`) has no key, so it falls through to the
232	    # modified-time ordering rather than crashing the `max` on a None vs str compare.
233	    keyed = [(f, m.group(1)) for f, m in matches if m.groups() and m.group(1) is not None]
234	    if keyed:
235	        return max(keyed, key=lambda fk: fk[1])[0].path
236	    return _most_recent([f for f, _ in matches])
237	
238	
239	def list_files(
240	    *, conn_type: str, config: dict[str, Any], prefix: str, secret: str
241	) -> list[FileRef]:
242	    """List objects/blobs under `prefix` on a flat-file datasource (live seam)."""
243	    if conn_type == "s3":
244	        cfg = S3Config.model_validate(config)
245	        paginator = _s3_client(cfg, secret).get_paginator("list_objects_v2")
246	        refs: list[FileRef] = []
247	        for page in paginator.paginate(Bucket=cfg.bucket, Prefix=prefix):
248	            for obj in page.get("Contents", []):
249	                refs.append(FileRef(path=obj["Key"], last_modified=obj.get("LastModified")))
250	        return refs
251	
252	    acfg = AdlsConfig.model_validate(config)
253	    client_az = _blob_service(acfg, secret)
254	    try:
255	        container = client_az.get_container_client(acfg.container)
256	        return [
257	            FileRef(path=blob.name, last_modified=getattr(blob, "last_modified", None))
258	            for blob in container.list_blobs(name_starts_with=prefix)
259	        ]
260	    finally:
261	        client_az.close()
262	
263	
264	def resolve_batch_file(
265	    *,
266	    conn_type: str,
267	    config: dict[str, Any],
268	    secret: str,
269	    prefix: str,
270	    pattern: str,
271	    strategy: str = "latest",
272	    batch: str | None = None,
273	) -> str:
274	    """List under `prefix`, then resolve the batch file path (list + `resolve_batch`)."""
275	    files = list_files(conn_type=conn_type, config=config, prefix=prefix, secret=secret)
276	    return resolve_batch(files, pattern=pattern, strategy=strategy, batch=batch)

=== RESULT status tiers/operational (models.py 26-40) ===
RUN_STATUSES = ("queued", "running", "succeeded", "failed", "cancelled")
# Result statuses. The four severity tiers (ADR 0005) are health-score-bearing —
# the score aggregate sums their weights over N. The two operational statuses
# (#122) are orthogonal: 'skip' = not evaluated, 'error' = evaluation threw
# (distinct from 'fail', a successful evaluation that breached). Operational
# statuses carry NO penalty weight and MUST be excluded from the health-score N
# (i.e. aggregate WHERE status IN the four tiers only).
_RESULT_SEVERITY_TIERS = ("pass", "warn", "fail", "critical")
_RESULT_OPERATIONAL_STATUSES = ("skip", "error")
RESULT_STATUSES = _RESULT_SEVERITY_TIERS + _RESULT_OPERATIONAL_STATUSES
# Monitor-kind discriminator (ADR 0012; `comparison` reserved by ADR 0014). v1
# only ever writes 'expectation'; the rest are constraint-valid but unused.
CHECK_KINDS = ("expectation", "freshness", "volume", "schema_drift", "anomaly", "comparison")
PIPELINE_RUN_STATUSES = ("queued", "running", "succeeded", "failed", "cancelled")
ORCHESTRATION_PROVIDERS = ("adf", "airflow")

) -> Suite:
    """Create a suite bound to an existing connection.

    Raises `SuiteConnectionInvalidError` (422) if the connection does not exist
    — caught here so a bad `connection_id` is a clean validation error, not a
    raw FK IntegrityError surfacing as 500. A provided ``target`` is validated
    against the connection's datasource type (422 if malformed); a suite may also
    be created targetless (NULL) and have a target set later via update.
    """
    connection = session.get(Connection, connection_id)
    if connection is None:
        raise SuiteConnectionInvalidError(
            "connection not found", detail={"connection_id": str(connection_id)}
        )
    if connection.type in ORCHESTRATION_PROVIDERS:
        # ADF/Airflow are orchestration providers, never suite datasources
        # (CLAUDE.md §4): a suite's connection is where its checks run. They
        # relate to suites only via trigger_bindings (trigger on pipeline success).
        raise SuiteConnectionInvalidError(
            "orchestration providers cannot be a suite's datasource; "
            "they trigger suites via trigger bindings",
            detail={"connection_id": str(connection_id), "type": connection.type},
        )
    if target is not None:
        run_target.validate_target(connection.type, target)
    suite = Suite(
        name=name,
        description=description,
        connection_id=connection_id,
        created_by=created_by,
        target=target,
    )
    session.add(suite)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(suite)
    log.info("suite_created", suite_id=str(suite.id), connection_id=str(connection_id))

## Proposed sequence (priority + dependency ordered)

**Phase 0 — Quick close (½ day)**
1. **#212** — add the rejection test (orchestration conn → 422 on create + import), close the issue. Pure verification + test.

**Phase 1 — Backend run-path completion** *(the "runs across all datasource types" half of the exit gate — highest priority)*
2. **A3 — Run-path `error`/`skip` emission (#122, P1).** Change `run_service` so a per-check exception yields a `Result(status='error')` instead of failing the whole run; emit `skip` for not-evaluated. Foundational — A4/A5 build on it.
3. **A4 — Flat-file batch resolution + run path (+ #147 cleanup, P1).** Wire `resolve_batch_file` into the target/worker so a `pattern`/`strategy` target resolves to a concrete path before read; missing batch → `skip`. Fold the #147 flat-file/profiler cleanup here.
4. **A5 — UC run path verify + integration test.** Runner exists; add end-to-end integration coverage, confirm `catalog.schema.table` resolution. Light.

**Phase 2 — Run lifecycle (progress + cancel)** *(unlocks the live-progress UI)*
5. **A1 — Run progress API.** Poll endpoint returning per-check live status off the run/result read model.
6. **A2 — Cancel run endpoint (+ #227 dispatch dedup, P3).** `cancelled` already in the enum; add Celery revoke + terminal transition. Fold the #227 create-queued-run/dispatch-failure dedup here since it touches the same dispatch shape.

**Phase 3 — Orchestration monitoring** *(independent; can run in parallel with Phases 1–2)*
7. **B1 — `GET /api/v1/orchestration/pipelines`.** `list_pipeline_runs` already exists in the service — provider-agnostic read endpoint.
8. **B2 — Gap recovery beat.** Startup + 30-min schedule extending the existing `poll_orchestration_runs`.

**Phase 4 — Scheduling backend** *(the implied prerequisite for "scheduling operational")*
9. **A7 — Scheduling backend.** Cron-schedule model + migration + CRUD API + Celery-beat dynamic dispatch of `run_suite`. Flag: needs a small design decision (DB-backed beat vs `celery-beat` scheduler).

**Phase 5 — Execution UI** *(depends on the above endpoints)*
10. **C1 — Run now panel** (POST endpoint already exists → pure UI).
11. **C2 — Live run progress UI** ← A1 + A2.
12. **C3 — Recent runs audit table** ← GET /runs + B1.
13. **C4 — Scheduled runs table** ← A7.
14. **A6 — Run history retention purge** (independent backend; can land any time).

Each numbered item = one PR (one-functionality-per-commit rule). Phases 1–2 and Phase 3 are parallelizable if you want; the critical path to the exit gate is **0 → Phase 1 → A1/A2 → Phase 4 → UI**.

1	"""Datasource adapter seam.
2	
3	Every datasource (Snowflake now; ADLS / S3 / Unity Catalog later) executes DQ
4	checks behind one ``CheckRunner`` interface that speaks GX-agnostic DTOs. The
5	GX-specific machinery lives entirely inside each adapter, so the run-service and
6	its tests depend only on the types here — never on Great Expectations internals.
7	This is also the seam that lets v1.1 swap GX for DQX on Unity Catalog (CLAUDE.md
8	§5) without rippling into the suite / check / result layer.
9	
10	`CheckSpec` goes in (a check pulled from the DB); `CheckOutcome` comes out, one
11	per check, shaped to map cleanly onto the `results` table columns. Adapters
12	translate GX results into these DTOs; tests provide a fake `CheckRunner` and
13	never touch a live datasource.
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	from dataclasses import dataclass
19	from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable
20	
21	from pydantic import BaseModel
22	
23	
24	@dataclass(frozen=True)
25	class CheckSpec:
26	    """One expectation to evaluate, sourced from a `checks` row.
27	
28	    `expectation_type` is the GX snake_case name (e.g.
29	    ``expect_column_values_to_not_be_null``); `kwargs` are its parameters
30	    (e.g. ``{"column": "id"}``). Adapters own the translation to the concrete
31	    GX expectation class.
32	    """
33	
34	    expectation_type: str
35	    kwargs: dict[str, Any]
36	
37	
38	@dataclass(frozen=True)
39	class CheckOutcome:
40	    """Result of one check, shaped for the `results` table.
41	
42	    `observed_value` / `expected_value` / `sample_failures` land in the
43	    matching JSONB columns. `sample_failures` may contain real data rows, so it
44	    is governed by the retention sweep and must only ever be logged through the
45	    PII-redacting structlog chain.
46	    """
47	
48	    expectation_type: str
49	    success: bool
50	    observed_value: dict[str, Any] | None = None
51	    expected_value: dict[str, Any] | None = None
52	    sample_failures: dict[str, Any] | None = None
53	
54	
55	@dataclass(frozen=True)
56	class SuiteOutcome:
57	    """Aggregate result of running a list of checks against one table."""
58	
59	    success: bool
60	    checks: list[CheckOutcome]
61	
62	
63	@runtime_checkable
64	class CheckRunner(Protocol):
65	    """Executes a set of checks against a single table and returns outcomes."""
66	
67	    def run_checks(
68	        self,
69	        *,
70	        table: str,
71	        schema: str | None,
72	        checks: list[CheckSpec],
73	    ) -> SuiteOutcome: ...
74	
75	
76	@runtime_checkable
77	class ConnectionAdapter(Protocol):
78	    """Per-datasource-type connection behaviour: config validation + live test.
79	
80	    The two things that vary across connection types (Snowflake now; ADF, ADLS,
81	    S3, Unity Catalog next) behind one interface, so connection-CRUD service code
82	    dispatches by ``connection.type`` and never branches on it. Each adapter owns
83	    its own pydantic config model; both methods take the raw config dict so the
84	    adapter is the single source of truth for that type's shape.
85	
86	    `validate_config` parses + validates a stored/incoming config (raising
87	    pydantic ``ValidationError`` on bad input) and returns the normalised model.
88	    `test` resolves connectivity against the live datasource using the config +
89	    its secret, raising on failure. Adapters never touch the DB or SecretStore —
90	    the caller resolves the secret and hands it in.
91	    """
92	
93	    def validate_config(self, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> BaseModel: ...
94	
95	    def test(self, raw: dict[str, Any], secret: str) -> None: ...
96

1	"""Shared Great Expectations machinery for the datasource `CheckRunner`s.
2	
3	The GX-version-specific translation — snake_case `expectation_type` → GX class,
4	and GX `ExpectationSuiteValidationResult` → our GX-agnostic `SuiteOutcome` DTOs —
5	is identical across datasources. It lives here so every runner (Snowflake table,
6	flat-file DataFrame, Unity Catalog later) reuses one implementation and the GX v1
7	API is pinned in a single place (CLAUDE.md §5 — GX has drifted across releases).
8	
9	Each runner only differs in how it builds the GX *batch* (a Snowflake table
10	asset vs an in-memory pandas asset); once it has a `batch_definition` it calls
11	`run_expectations`, which registers the suite + validation definition and maps
12	the result. Tests exercise these pure parts with constructed GX results and a
13	canned DataFrame — no live datasource required.
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	from typing import Any
19	
20	import great_expectations as gx
21	import great_expectations.expectations as gxe
22	
23	from backend.app.datasources.base import CheckOutcome, CheckSpec, SuiteOutcome
24	
25	# GX result keys that describe failing rows — copied into CheckOutcome.sample_failures.
26	# These may contain real data, so they only ever reach logs via the redactor.
27	_SAMPLE_KEYS = ("partial_unexpected_list", "unexpected_count", "unexpected_percent")
28	
29	# GX injects internal bookkeeping keys into expectation_config.kwargs at run time
30	# (e.g. batch_id); strip them so expected_value persists only the check's own
31	# parameters.
32	_GX_INTERNAL_KWARGS = frozenset({"batch_id"})
33	
34	
35	class UnknownExpectationError(ValueError):
36	    """Raised when a check's expectation_type has no matching GX expectation."""
37	
38	
39	def _expectation_class_name(expectation_type: str) -> str:
40	    """snake_case GX type → PascalCase class name.
41	
42	    ``expect_column_values_to_not_be_null`` → ``ExpectColumnValuesToNotBeNull``.
43	    """
44	    return "".join(part.title() for part in expectation_type.split("_"))
45	
46	
47	def _to_gx_expectation(spec: CheckSpec) -> Any:
48	    class_name = _expectation_class_name(spec.expectation_type)
49	    expectation_cls = getattr(gxe, class_name, None)
50	    if expectation_cls is None:
51	        raise UnknownExpectationError(
52	            f"Unknown expectation_type {spec.expectation_type!r} (no gx class {class_name!r})"
53	        )
54	    return expectation_cls(**spec.kwargs)
55	
56	
57	def _extract_sample_failures(result: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
58	    sample = {key: result[key] for key in _SAMPLE_KEYS if key in result}
59	    return sample or None
60	
61	
62	def _expected_value(kwargs: Any) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
63	    cleaned = {key: value for key, value in dict(kwargs).items() if key not in _GX_INTERNAL_KWARGS}
64	    return cleaned or None
65	
66	
67	def to_suite_outcome(gx_result: Any) -> SuiteOutcome:
68	    """Map a GX ExpectationSuiteValidationResult onto our GX-agnostic DTO.
69	
70	    Kept GX-translation-only (no datasource specifics) so it is unit-testable
71	    with a constructed GX result, no live datasource required.
72	    """
73	    outcomes: list[CheckOutcome] = []
74	    for check_result in gx_result.results:
75	        config = check_result.expectation_config
76	        detail: dict[str, Any] = check_result.result or {}
77	        observed = (
78	            {"observed_value": detail["observed_value"]} if "observed_value" in detail else None
79	        )
80	        outcomes.append(
81	            CheckOutcome(
82	                expectation_type=config.type,
83	                success=bool(check_result.success),
84	                observed_value=observed,
85	                expected_value=_expected_value(config.kwargs) if config.kwargs else None,
86	                sample_failures=_extract_sample_failures(detail),
87	            )
88	        )
89	    return SuiteOutcome(success=bool(gx_result.success), checks=outcomes)
90	
91	
92	def run_expectations(
93	    context: Any,
94	    *,
95	    batch_definition: Any,
96	    checks: list[CheckSpec],
97	    name: str,
98	    batch_parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
99	) -> SuiteOutcome:
100	    """Register the suite + validation definition for `batch_definition` and run.
101	
102	    The shared tail of every runner: GX 1.x requires the suite and validation
103	    definition to be registered on the (ephemeral, per-run) context before
104	    ``run()``. `batch_parameters` carries the in-memory DataFrame for a pandas
105	    asset; it stays `None` for an asset that resolves its own batch (a SQL table),
106	    matching a bare ``run()``.
107	    """
108	    suite = context.suites.add(
109	        gx.ExpectationSuite(
110	            name=name,
111	            expectations=[_to_gx_expectation(check) for check in checks],
112	        )
113	    )
114	    validation_definition = context.validation_definitions.add(
115	        gx.ValidationDefinition(name=f"vd-{name}", data=batch_definition, suite=suite)
116	    )
117	    result = validation_definition.run(batch_parameters=batch_parameters, result_format="COMPLETE")
118	    return to_suite_outcome(result)
119	
```

> AGENT

Confirmed GX 1.17.2 behavior — this is the crux of #122's `error` path:

- A per-check exception (e.g. missing column) → that check's `ExpectationValidationResult` has `success=False` **and** `exception_info` populated; **sibling checks still run**.
- **`exception_info` has two shapes**: errored → keyed by `MetricConfigurationID` strings, each `{raised_exception: True, exception_message, ...}`; clean → flat `{raised_exception: False, ...}`. The detector must handle both.

So today an *errored* check is silently recorded as `fail` (success=False → severity derives `fail`) — that's exactly the misclassification #122 fixes. Let me check the health-score query and the run_service tests before designing.

1	"""Severity post-processing — derive a result's tier from check thresholds.
2	
3	The single home for the ADR-0005 tier derivation + the ADR-0012 `metric_value`
4	extraction, kept pure (no DB, no GX) so the semantics live in one place: if we
5	ever switch from banding the *unexpected fraction* to banding the *raw observed
6	value* (ADR 0016 approach B), only this module changes.
7	
8	Model (ADR 0016, approach A):
9	- `metric_value` = the GX **unexpected percent** (0-100): how badly the rule was
10	  violated. 0 = clean, higher = worse. It is the SQL-aggregatable badness scalar
11	  (ADR 0012) and the quantity the thresholds band.
12	- When a check has thresholds, they are the user's severity policy and they
13	  fully determine the tier — overriding GX's binary success (e.g. a check with
14	  `mostly=0.99` that GX fails at 0.5% unexpected resolves to `pass` if the user's
15	  `warn` threshold is 1%). The stored `metric_value` keeps this transparent.
16	- No thresholds set, or no metric to band (aggregate checks like row_count that
17	  produce no unexpected fraction) → binary `pass`/`fail` from GX success
18	  (ADR 0005 binary fallback).
19	"""
20	
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
24	from typing import Any
25	
26	from backend.app.datasources.base import CheckOutcome
27	
28	# GX key carrying the violated-row fraction (0-100), copied into sample_failures
29	# by the runner. This is the badness scalar the thresholds band.
30	_UNEXPECTED_PERCENT_KEY = "unexpected_percent"
31	
32	
33	def extract_metric(outcome: CheckOutcome) -> Decimal | None:
34	    """The numeric badness scalar for a check, or None if it has none.
35	
36	    Reads the GX unexpected-percent from the outcome's sample detail. Computed at
37	    run time and persisted to `results.metric_value`, so it survives the later
38	    sample-failures retention purge (the durable scalar the dashboard trends).
39	    Uses ``Decimal(str(...))`` so a float like ``0.5`` lands as exact ``0.5`` in
40	    the NUMERIC column rather than its binary expansion.
41	    """
42	    sample: dict[str, Any] | None = outcome.sample_failures
43	    if not sample or _UNEXPECTED_PERCENT_KEY not in sample:
44	        return None
45	    raw = sample[_UNEXPECTED_PERCENT_KEY]
46	    if raw is None:
47	        return None
48	    try:
49	        metric = Decimal(str(raw))
50	    except (InvalidOperation, ValueError, TypeError):
51	        return None
52	    # GX can emit NaN/inf — e.g. unexpected_percent on an empty table is 0/0
53	    # (the same reason run_service runs a NaN->null sanitizer). A non-finite
54	    # Decimal slips past the parse but would make every threshold comparison
55	    # False (silently 'pass') or raise mid-run; treat it as "no bandable
56	    # metric" so derive_status falls back to binary pass/fail.
57	    return metric if metric.is_finite() else None
58	
59	
60	def derive_status(
61	    *,
62	    success: bool,
63	    metric_value: Decimal | None,
64	    warn_threshold: Decimal | None,
65	    fail_threshold: Decimal | None,
66	    critical_threshold: Decimal | None,
67	) -> str:
68	    """Resolve a result's tier (`pass`/`warn`/`fail`/`critical`), ADR 0005.
69	
70	    Higher `metric_value` is worse; thresholds are ordered (warn ≤ fail ≤
71	    critical) and any unset threshold is skipped (treated as +∞). Falls back to
72	    binary pass/fail when the check carries no thresholds, or carries thresholds
73	    but produced no bandable metric.
74	    """
75	    no_thresholds = warn_threshold is None and fail_threshold is None and critical_threshold is None
76	    if no_thresholds or metric_value is None:
77	        return "pass" if success else "fail"
78	
79	    if critical_threshold is not None and metric_value >= critical_threshold:
80	        return "critical"
81	    if fail_threshold is not None and metric_value >= fail_threshold:
82	        return "fail"
83	    if warn_threshold is not None and metric_value >= warn_threshold:
84	        return "warn"
85	    return "pass"
86	
```

2	
3	No database or GX: a fake Session records what would be persisted, model

5	canned outcomes (or raises). This keeps the service's lifecycle + mapping logic
6	under test independent of Postgres and Snowflake.
7	"""
